title: Knight Forks
concept: One knight, two targets. The knight is the sneakiest fork in the jungle.

glossary.definition: One piece attacking two enemy pieces at the same time. Your opponent can only save one of them.

summary: Before every move, ask: can my knight jump to a square that hits two things? A fork with check is the best kind, because the king must move first.

narration: Black's bishop runs away from your knight. Fair enough, but that bishop was also guarding c7. Keep an eye on that square.
Knight to c7, check! From one square it attacks the king on e8 AND the rook on a8. That's a fork.
Check must be answered first, so the king steps aside. Nobody has time to save the rook.
Knight takes the rook. One move, two targets, and a whole rook in your pocket.

guided.hint: Your knight on d5 has a jump that gives check. Which of those squares also reaches something valuable?
guided.explanation: Knight to e7 is check, and it also hits the queen on c8. Black's knight on c6 was the only guard of e7, and it just wandered off. The king has to move, so the queen falls.

wrong.d5b4: Taking the knight is fine, but there's a bigger fish. Look for a check that also attacks the queen.

guided.hint: Black's pawn just left f7, and pawns can never step back. Which piece can land on the hole it left?
guided.explanation: Knight to f7 is check, and from f7 the knight also eyes the queen on d8. The king runs, the queen is lost. When a pawn steps forward, it leaves a hole behind it for good.

wrong.g5e6: Knight to e6 attacks the queen, but she just walks away. Make the fork a check, so she doesn't get the time.

guided.hint: You're Black this time. White's bishop moved, so which square did it stop guarding? Your knight might like it.
guided.explanation: Knight to e2 is check, and it also attacks the queen on c3. White's bishop used to guard e2, but it went chasing your b7 pawn. The king moves, the queen falls.

wrong.d4f3: Knight to f3 is check, but the g2 pawn simply eats your knight. A fork only works if the forking piece is safe.

wrong.c7c4: Grabbing the bishop is nice, but your knight could win the queen with check. Checks first!

wrong.d4f3: Knight to f3 is check, but two white pawns can capture on f3. Find a fork square nobody guards.

wrong.f5d4: Taking the pawn wins a little. Your knight has a square that hits the queen and a rook at once.

wrong.e4f6: Knight to f6 is check, but the g7 pawn takes your knight. Forks must land on safe squares.
